questions.question: How many nations (including EOR and ROC teams) participated in the 2020 Summer Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**206.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The total number of participating nations in the** 2020 Summer Olympics** was **206**, which includes **11 athletes **from the** EOR team **and **335 athletes** from the ROC team.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **EOR** stands for the **"Refugee Olympic Team",** which was established in **2016** to provide a platform for athletes who have been displaced from their home countries due to** war, conflict, or other reasons.**
 
• **ROC** stands for the **"Russian Olympic Committee"**, which was formed after **Russia was banned** from participating in the Olympics due to a state-sponsored doping scandal.
 
• **Athletes from Russia **were allowed to compete under the** ROC flag** and anthem, but **not** under the Russian flag or anthem.

questions.question: It connects all types of computers across the world. Which communication technology is being spoken about here?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Internet.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Internet **is a **global network of computers** that enables communication and data exchange between them.
 
• It connects **computers, servers, routers,** and other devices across the world.
 
• Internet uses various communication protocols such as** TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP,** etc. to ensure **seamless data transfer** between different types of computers and networks.
 
• With the help of Internet, users can access a wide range of **services and applications** such as **email, social media, online shopping, video conferencing, cloud computing**, and much more.
 
• Internet has revolutionized the way people **communicate, work, learn, and entertain** themselves.
 
• It has become an** integral part **of our daily lives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pager** is a **wireless communication device** that receives and displays messages, usually in the form of text.

 
 
• It was popular in the **1990s** but has become obsolete with the advent of smartphones and mobile internet.
 
 
 
• **Post cards **are a form of **traditional mail **that carries a **short message or image **on a small piece of paper or cardboard.
 
 
• They are still used for **personal and business correspondence**, but their usage has declined due to the rise of email and instant messaging.
 
 
 
• **Cable** refers to a **physical medium of transmitting data and signals,** such as coaxial cable, fiber optic cable, or Ethernet cable.
 
 
• It is used in various communication technologies such as** cable TV, broadband internet, and LAN** (Local Area Network).

questions.question: After the passage of which Constitutional Amendment Act, are there now six fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment in 1978.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** is the Constitutional Amendment Act that reduced the number of fundamental rights from seven to six by removing the right to property as a fundamental right.
 
• **102nd Amendment in 1996** was related to the implementation of the **Mandal Commission report** on reservations in jobs and education for **Other Backward Classes (OBCs).**
 
• 44th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as the Constitution of India was adopted in 1950 and the first amendment was made in 1951.
 
• 11th Amendment in 1952 **does not exist** as there were only three amendments made in 1951, which were related to the salaries of the President, Vice-President, and Governors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights** are a set of basic rights that are guaranteed to all citizens under the Constitution of India.
 
• These include the** right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, right to life and liberty,** and** cultural and educational rights.**
 
• The **Right to Education **was added as the** sixth fundamental right** by the** 44th Amendment in 1978**, which made it the responsibility of the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
• The **Right to Education** was further strengthened by the** 86th Amendment in 2002**, which made education a fundamental right for children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
 
• This amendment also made it mandatory for private schools to **reserve 25% of their seats** for children from economically weaker sections.

questions.question: Which of the following Metals of Harappan civilization got from present-day Rajasthan and Oman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** was one of the** main metals **used by the **Harappan civilization,** and they sourced it from present-day **Rajasthan and Oman**.
 
• The Harappans used copper for various purposes, including making** tools, weapons, and ornaments.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tin:**

 
 
• While tin was not sourced from Rajasthan or Oman, it was an **important metal **for the Harappans.
 
• They used it to make** bronze,** which is an alloy of copper and tin.
 
• Bronze was used to make a variety of objects, including** tools, weapons, and statues.**
 
 
 
• **Gold and silver:**
 
 
• These precious metals were **not as common** as copper and tin in Harappan society.
 
• Gold was likely used for **jewelry and decorative objects**, while silver may have been used as a form of currency.
 
• The Harappans were skilled at working with these metals and produced** intricate jewelry **and other objects using techniques such as filigree and granulation.

questions.question: ___________war took place during fourth five year plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India -Pakistan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The fourth five-year plan was implemented in India from** 1969 to 1974,** and during this period,** India and Pakistan **fought the war of **1971.**
 
• The war was fought mainly over the** issue of East Pakistan, **which later became **Bangladesh.**
 
• India supported the independence movement of East Pakistan, and Pakistan **opposed it.**
 
• The war lasted for **13 days **and ended with the surrender of around 90,000 Pakistani soldiers.
 
• It resulted in the** liberation of East Pakistan** and the **formation of Bangladesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-China war:**

 
 
• The Indo-China war was fought between India and China in **1962** over the **border dispute** between the two countries.
 
• It resulted in a defeat for India and led to a **strained relationship **between the two countries for many years. 
 
 
 
• **World War II:**
 
 
• World War II was a global conflict that lasted from **1939 to 1945.**
 
• It involved most of the world's major powers and resulted in the** deaths of millions** of people.
 
• The war ended with the defeat of **Germany and Japan** and the emergence of the **United States** and the **Soviet Union** as superpowers.
 
 
 
• **World War I:**
 
 
• World War I was a global war that lasted from **1914 to 1918**.
 
• It involved most of the world's great powers and resulted in the** deaths of millions **of people.

questions.question: In India, the Industrial Policy Resolution was passed in the year _______ for the first time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1948.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948** was the first comprehensive policy statement of the Government of India regarding the **industrial development** of the country.
 
• The resolution aimed to lay the foundation of a **socialistic pattern of society** by promoting the **growth of industries **in the **public sector **and regulating the private sector.
 
• The resolution also emphasized the need for the state to take an active role in the development of infrastructure, such as** power, transport, and communication,** which are essential for the growth of industries.
 
• The resolution was later replaced by the **Industrial Policy of 1956**, which further strengthened the role of the public sector in industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1949** was the year when the **Planning Commission** was established in India, which played a significant role in the **economic planning** of the country.
 
• **1946** was the year when the **Interim Government of India** was formed, which was responsible for the administration of the country until the transfer of power to the** Indian government in 1947.**
 
• **1947 **was the year when India gained **independence from British rule**, which marked a significant turning point in the history of the country.
 
 
• The year also saw the **partition of India and the creation of Pakistan**.

questions.question: __________is defined as the body’s ability to function efficiently and effectively in work and leisure activities, to be healthy, to resist diseases and to meet emergency situations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**physical fitness.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Physical fitness** is the correct answer as it encompasses all aspects of the body's ability to function** efficiently and effectively** in **work and leisure** activities, to be healthy, to **resist diseases** and to meet** emergency situations.**
 
• **Aerobic fitness **refers to the ability of the body to** use oxygen efficiently** during physical activity and is a component of physical fitness.
 
• **Muscular endurance** refers to the ability of the muscles to perform **repetitive movements** for an **extended period of time** and is also a component of physical fitness.
 
• **Mental fitness,** while important for overall health, is **not specifically** related to the body's physical ability to function efficiently and effectively in work and leisure activities.
 
• **Maintaining physical fitness **can lead to a **decreased risk of chronic diseases **such as** heart disease, diabetes, and obesity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical fitness **is often measured through various tests such as **cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, and flexibility.**
 
• **Regular physical activity,** such as exercise, is a key factor in maintaining physical fitness.
 
• Poor physical fitness can lead to a **decreased quality of life **and an increased risk of** chronic diseases.**
 
• It is important to consult with a healthcare professional before** beginning any new exercise program** to ensure safety and effectiveness.

questions.question: National Income = C (household consumption) + G(_________) + I (investment expense) + NX (net exports).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**government expenditure**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National income** is calculated by adding up the **total expenditures** in the economy, which includes **government spending.**
 
• Government expenditure refers to the** amount of money **spent by the government on** goods and services,** such as** infrastructure, defense, education, and healthcare.** 
 
• It is an important component of **national income**, as it represents the government's contribution to the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Household consumption**, represented by the **variable C, **refers to the amount of money spent by households on **goods and services.**

 
 
• It is the largest component of** national income,** as it represents the spending of the **majority of the population.**
 
 
 
• **Investment expenses**, represented by the **variable I**, refers to the amount of money spent by **businesses on capital goods**, such as **machinery, equipment, and buildings.**
 
 
• It is an important component of **national income**, as it represents the investment in the **economy's productive capacity**.
 
 
 
• **Net exports**, represented by the **variable NX, **refers to the difference between the value of a country's **exports and imports**.
 
 
• It is a measure of the **country's trade balance** and represents the amount of income earned from exports minus the amount spent on imports.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to Indian in January ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1915.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** returned to India in **January 1915.**
 
• He returned from** South Africa **where he had spent over two decades fighting for the** rights of Indians.**
 
• His return marked the beginning of his active involvement in the **Indian freedom struggle.**
 
• He played a key role in organizing various movements, including the** Non-cooperation Movement** and the **Salt Satyagraha, **which eventually led to India's independence from British rule.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of** non-violent resistance, or Satyagraha,** inspired many leaders around the world, including **Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In** 1911**, Gandhi was still in South Africa and was actively involved in the Indian community's struggle for **civil rights.**
 
• In **1907**, Gandhi was still in South Africa and was leading the Indian community's resistance against the **discriminatory laws** imposed by the colonial government.
 
• In **1919**, Gandhi was already in India and was leading the **Non-cooperation Movement** against the British rule.
